name: Відкриті шахи (2)
description:
In discovered checks it is important to make sure that the back piece cannot be taken.

But in example 1 it does not really matter.

In the other examples, White has to pay better attention. White has two ways to deliver a discovered attack. But only one is good. If he picks the wrong way, he loses points.

In example 2 White moves the front piece, attacking the enemy queen. But that’s not all. The front piece is now protecting the back piece. Smart move!

In example 3 White uses a different trick.
He places the front piece between the enemy queen and his back piece. The back piece is safe from taking.
White attacks the queen and checks the king. A nice way to win points!

What do you have to do?
Use a discovered check to win points.

examples.pgn: {(%csl Rd1)(%cal Gd1d7,Gd4f3)} 1. Nf3+ {[%csl Rd7,Rg5]} Bxd1 2. Nxg5 *
examples.text:
If White follows the green arrow, Black is in check.
At the same time, Black’s queen is attacked by the knight.
Black can get out of check by capturing the rook (5 points).
No big deal.
In turn, White’s knight can take the queen (9 points). 9 -5 = 4 points profit.

White can attack the knight in two ways.
Following the red arrow is not smart.
It might seem so, since it checks the king and attacks the queen at the same time.
But Black can easily get out of this. By taking the rook with his queen, check is gone and the queen is safe.
Black has even won 5 points!

It is much better for White to follow the green arrow.
Again, Black’s king is in check and his queen is attacked.
But now White’s rook is guarded.
Black may take, but White’s queen will recapture.
This wins White 9 – 5 = 4 points!

examples.pgn: {(%csl Rd1)(%cal Gd5f3,Rd5f7,Gh5d1)} 1. Bf3+ {[%csl Rd7,Rh5]} Ke7 2. Bxh5 *
examples.text:
Now, White has to pay better attention.
White’s bishop can attack the queen in two ways.
Following the red arrow is not a good idea.
Black’s queen will take the rook to get out of check.

It is much better to follow the green arrow.
The bishop moves between the queen and the rook.
Now, Black cannot take the rook.
Black needs to find another way to get out of check.
And White wins a queen!

texts: Look for pieces aligned. This offers tactical chances!
